verifiable-quality-gates.why: the change adds three new gates and promotes a fourth, so each ships a committed test that runs the REAL gate and discriminates: no-op the gate and its test goes red (verified by stubbing each to process.exit(0) and re-running), and each gate fails closed on an empty/missing surface so it can never pass while scanning nothing.
verifiable-quality-gates.what: wrote discrimination tests for the three new wrapper gates (happy, real-violation, whole-tree-walk, and fail-closed exit-2 cases) and mutation-proved each; verify-check-discrimination (the mutation gate itself) is promoted to a consumer-gate with its pinned testSha256.
quotes: A quality gate is only worth the failures it catches

architectural-decision-records.why: promoting four helpers to consumer-gates is an architecturally significant, lasting decision (it changes what the skills ship as enforced), so it is recorded in an ADR committed with the code.
architectural-decision-records.what: wrote ADR-0113 recording the decision, the four considered options and why option 1 (a wrapper per tool that reuses the one oracle) was chosen, the patch-not-minor semver rationale, and the honest limits.
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

judge-arch.why: a change that adds gates and schema-shaped manifest entries got a fresh-context review of every changed file against the four questions before done, with detection re-implementation, fail-closed completeness, secret handling, and gate vacuity as the adversarial focus.
judge-arch.what: dispatched a fresh-context subagent review covering all 12 files; it returned the full matrix and one finding (F1, a secret-value leak on the fail-closed path) which was fixed; the review is recorded in docs/arch-reviews/entries/.
quotes: Architectural drift is cheap to add and expensive to trace later

skeptical-audit.why: the claims-grounded gate IS this skill's evidence discipline turned into a repo gate (it runs claim-lint --strict over a whole findings surface), and the SKILL.md evidence-contract row is corrected to match the new wiring without overstating it.
skeptical-audit.what: built check-claims-grounded.mjs (walks a configured surface, spawns the real claim-lint per file, fails closed on an empty surface) and updated the evidence-contract row to say claim-lint is wired as the claims-grounded consumer-gate, not yet installed/run in a consumer.
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: the promoted gates are new behavior with operator and agent audiences, so the use cases (happy, negative, edge/fail-closed, and the security no-print case) are enumerated as tagged Gherkin and wired into the executable BDD suite.
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: added features/repo-process/consumer-gate-promotion.feature (six tagged scenarios) and executable steps that spawn the real wrapper gates; npm run test:bdd runs and reconciles them (167 scenarios, all pass).
quotes: the only way to keep a contract honest is to write it down as executable scenarios

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: the secret-leak gate belongs to this skill (leak-check is its worked example of a tested oracle); promoting it adds the wrapper plus the integration-level test that spawns the real gate across a fixture surface.
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: built check-secret-leaks.mjs (resolves secret values from named env vars, scans build output, reports the env-var name never the value) and its discrimination test covering the leak, whole-tree-walk, and fail-closed cases.
quotes: the more high-level you get the fewer tests you should have

usability-ux-universal-design.why: the readability gate belongs to this skill (readability.mjs measures the reading grade of user-facing prose); promoting it adds the wrapper that holds a whole doc surface at or below a configured grade.
usability-ux-universal-design.what: built check-readability.mjs (walks a configured user-facing surface, spawns the real readability --max-grade per file, fails closed on an empty surface) and its discrimination test.
quotes: Words are UI, and people skim rather than read

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: the secret-leak gate handles secrets, so it was threat-modeled: values come from the CI environment (never the committed config), are never written to disk, and are never printed (the F1 fix removed the one path that could echo a value); a @security scenario covers the no-print behavior.
owasp-secure-coding-bdd.what: designed the secret handling (env-var names in config, values from process.env, one-secret-at-a-time so a hit maps to a name without printing the value, child output withheld on the fail-closed path) and added the @security 'secret-leak-caught' scenario asserting the value is not printed.
quotes: A threat with no countermeasure is a vulnerability, not a decision

pattern-selector.why: no feature, class, module, or data flow selects a GoF/enterprise pattern; the gate-reuses-the-tool-by-spawn approach follows the existing check-axe-results/run-axe precedent and is recorded in ADR-0113's options, not a new pattern.

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: no system topology, database schema, service, or integration changes; the change adds self-contained CLI gate scripts and manifest classification.

release-deployment-safety.why: nothing is deployed or migrated; consumerRequiredGates are classified only and reach a consumer later through genesis, not this change. The version bump is a separate release PR.

sre-operational-readiness.why: no running service, endpoint, SLO, or alert; these are CI gate scripts.

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: no personal or regulated data and no storage/retention/backup surface; the secret-leak gate scans build output for secret values but stores and retains nothing.

arch-encode.why: no new greppable arch-gate rule is encoded; these are discipline gates owned by their skills, not arch-gate fitness rules, and the judge-arch review found no recurring drift to ratchet.

universal-accessibility-wcag.why: no user interface; the readability gate measures prose grade but renders nothing.

universal-browser-device-support.why: no browser or device surface; the scripts are Node CLIs.
